series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

evidence.sentence:  Australia reaffirms its ambitious economy-wide target to reduce greenhouse emissions to by 26 - 28% below 2005 levels by 2030, and will exceed it by up to 9 percentage points.
On a point in time basis, Australia emissions in 2030 are projected to be 30-38% below 2005 levels.

label.text: Cumulative net national emissions (2030 multi-year target)

progress.text: Remaining emissions budget is 3,505.63 Mt CO2-e as at 2022. This means that Australia is 20% of the way through its 2030 multi-year target commitment period and has generated emissions equivalent to 20% of that target’s emissions budget.

title.text: 4. Structured summary: Tracking progress made in implementing and achieving the NDC under Article 4 of the Paris Agreement a

progress.text: In 2022, Australia’s net national emissions were 29% below 2005 levels. Australia’s emissions need to fall by a further 14 percentage points to meet its 2030 single year target of 43% below 2005 levels.

title.text: 4. Structured summary: Tracking progress made in implementing and achieving the NDC under Article 4 of the Paris Agreement a

as_written.text: Net national emissions reported for the most recent year published in Australia’s latest annual National Inventory Report.

progress.text: In 2022, Australia’s net national emissions were 432.62 Mt CO2-e, representing a 1.4% reduction on net national emissions reported for the previous year 2021 (438.75 Mt CO2-e).

target_text.text:
2030 multi-year target: absolute economy-wide emissions reduction commitment to reduce net national emissions to 43% below 2005 levels over 10 years from 2021 to 2030, implemented as an emissions budget.
2030 single-year target: absolute economy-wide emission reduction commitment to reduce net national emissions to 43% below 2005 levels in 2030.
2050 single-year target: absolute economy-wide emissions reduction commitment to achieve net zero national emissions in 2050.

emissions_profile.$note: Headline totals are OWID only. OWID's CO₂ sub-totals are fossil/industrial CO₂ by fuel, not a full sectoral GHG breakdown, and do not sum to total_mtco2e. DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is Australia’s second NDC, filed 2025-09-18. 77 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (31). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 781.2 MtCO₂e, DS-35 609.9 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 4 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 67.9 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 26% to 28% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to 2005 levels It was classed unconditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.1°C under SSP1-2.6 to +4.27°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
